payload.title: Port app policy hooks to the Rust authz pipeline (RBAC + entitlement write gating)
payload.description:
The TS @fricken/server ran the authz pipeline as: baseline -> APP POLICY HOOKS -> grant relaxation. The Rust `authz::decide` pipeline has no hook stage (baseline -> grant relaxation only); `routes/objects.rs` notes "App policy hooks are FR-245 and not wired here." So an app cannot supply custom write authorization on the Rust server.

Validated against Zavro (@zavro/backend), whose two policy hooks enforce things the schema/owner-scope/grants model cannot express:
1. RBAC — a role x action x resource-type WRITE matrix; role is derived from the principal's handle (roleForUserId), then rbacDenyReason(role, action, type) denies the write.
2. Entitlement — deny a module-gated object WRITE when the acting company (resolved via Membership at decision time, needs STORE ACCESS) lacks the required installed module.

Both are write-side + tightening-only (deny, never grant); entitlement needs the store at decision time.

Scope: add a hook stage to the Rust authz pipeline matching the TS PolicyHook contract ({ principal, action, resource:{kind,name,key,ownerId,tenantId}, context } -> { allow, reason, publicMessage }), tightening-only, runnable on allow, first-deny-wins, with store access for data-dependent hooks. Registerable via BootSeams/AppDefinition.

Refinement: RBAC (role x action x type) is common enough that a NATIVE declarative primitive (role claims on the principal + a schema-level write-role matrix) could cover the common case with zero custom code — consider shipping that alongside the raw hook. Blocks any extensible downstream app (Zavro) from running its authorization model on the Rust server.
